director_mandate_binding.binding_question: On the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate, over a multi-host pool whose DEEP (hop >= 3) state-item sampling frame is CERTIFIED to exist before freeze (>= 2 distinct hosts/engines, >= 3 DEEP items per engine, >= 10 total), what fraction of those DEEP items is reachable in <= K = 3 fresh-agent GETs using ANY of the five frozen site-native discovery channels (robots.txt sitemap directives, sitemap.xml, on-site search/query URLs, RSS/Atom feeds, JSON-LD/structured-data enumeration) -- with a preregistered materiality threshold on >= 2 engines deciding whether shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier (persistence of paths is not a core optimization target; effort moves to discovery and substrate expansion) versus fresh deep-instance acquisition remaining path-bound with a computable persistence break-even surface.

question: On the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate frozen by EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378, over a frozen 4-engine pool of DEEP (shortest-path hop in {3,4,5,6}) state-carrying items (a page whose HTML contains >=1 named <input>/<select>), what fraction of those items is reachable in <=K=3 fresh-agent GETs (1 discovery GET + 1 item-page GET + 1 spare) via ANY of the five frozen site-native discovery channels (ROBOTS_SITEMAP, SITEMAP_XML, ON_SITE_SEARCH, RSS_ATOM, JSON_LD) -- measured per engine with a preregistered materiality threshold 0.50 on >=2 distinct host engines?

hypothesis.H1: DISCOVERY_COLLAPSES_DEPTH: on >=2 distinct host engines, >=0.50 of admitted DEEP state items are reachable in <=K=3 GETs via at least one frozen site-native discovery channel, so shortest-path hop is not a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier and path/procedure persistence is not the primary optimization target.
hypothesis.H0: DEPTH_REMAINS_BARRIER: on fewer than 2 engines does the per-engine reachable fraction reach 0.50; fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound and persistence retains a depth-dependent amortization surface with a computable break-even.

falsifier.denominator: 40 admitted DEEP state items across 4 distinct host engines (10 per engine; exact URL list frozen in target_pool.admitted_items)
falsifier.positive_branch: Let E = number of available host engines with discovery_reachable_fraction_per_engine >= 0.50 (fraction = count(admitted items of that engine reachable via ANY channel within K=3 GETs) / admitted count of that engine = /10). SUPPORTS iff E >= 2. E=2 requires BOTH vitepress.dev (page-level sitemap, 272 locs) AND nix.dev (static search index, 1933 doc_urls; sitemap excludes /manual/) to enumerate their frozen frame items; both engines' per-item membership is genuinely open at DESIGN (only aggregate channel scope facts are frozen). E=1 (MIXED) and E=0 (FALSIFIES) remain arithmetically reachable: a live sitemap/search-index is not a witness that any specific admitted item appears in it.
falsifier.negative_branch: FALSIFIES iff E = 0; MIXED iff E = 1. Both branches imply the primary metric is well-defined (denominator 40, never 0); per-engine denominators are 10, never 0.
falsifier.structural_floors_disclosed: doc.rust-lang.org is a certified structural floor (sitemap.txt has exactly 3 version roots, none cargo; /sitemap.xml 404; book searchindex has 0 cargo-prefix entries) with expected fraction 0/10; rust-lang.github.io is a certified structural floor (no robots, no sitemap; async-book searchindex covers 3 of 10 frame items -> structural max 3/10 = 0.30 < 0.50). These floors calibrate the measurement machinery's negative end and cannot force either outcome: E is decided by the two live engines, whose per-item membership is not frozen.

B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS.description: Frozen item-blind same-host document-order link-following BFS (RED arm of EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378): number of HTTP GET requests issued before an admitted item page is first fetched, and its hop depth.
B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS.identifiable: Computed at EXECUTE on the SAME frozen admitted item set by re-running the frozen BFS (B=250, D=6, same-host static-<a>, document order) once per seed; deterministic on a stable site, with temporal drift recorded. The DESIGN-time BFS that certified the frame used the same frozen policy (certified_bfs2.json).

B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY.role: theoretical O(1) lower bound when the item URL is already known
B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY.description: One GET to the already-known item page URL (RACQ_URL of EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378).

B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT.role: contextual (NOT a comparator in the primary decision)
B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT.description: Persisted shortest-path replay cost hop+1 measured in the parent EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 on a single-engine mdBook pool. Recorded as inherited context only; explicitly NOT re-measured here and NOT used to compute the primary metric.
B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT.identifiable: Analytically defined; labeled inherited context; never paired with this experiment's discovery metric.

positive_control.description: At least one frozen site-native discovery channel must be probeable and return parsable same-host URL content (a non-empty parsed same-host URL set) on at least one host in the frozen pool, verified live during DESIGN.
positive_control.pass_criterion: At least one of the five channels yields a 2xx response whose parsed same-host URL set is non-empty on at least one host; verified in pre_freeze_control_certificate.channel_liveness.
positive_control.aggregate_only_note: This control is INSTRUMENT liveness only and is reported AGGREGATELY: per-host channel URL-set sizes (272 locs vitepress.dev sitemap.xml, 58 locs nix.dev sitemap.xml + 1933 doc_urls searchindex.js, 3 lines doc.rust-lang.org sitemap.txt, 0 on every channel for rust-lang.github.io). DESIGN deliberately does NOT compute, and the certificate deliberately does NOT contain, any per-item or per-engine reachability witness. The confirmatory per-engine fractions are measured only at EXECUTE.
positive_control.observed_pre_freeze: Aggregate channel liveness verified live 2026-10-10 (final_channels.json, final_scope.json): see pre_freeze_control_certificate.design_probe_evidence.channel_aggregates.

null_control.description: Per host, two frozen synthetic identifiers that do not exist are probed through the parsed URL sets of the discovery channels and by direct item-page fetch. They must yield zero discovered URLs and 404 on the item page, across all hosts.
null_control.pass_criterion: For all hosts and channels: 0 synthetic URLs discovered AND every synthetic item page returns 404.
null_control.purpose: Validates that the channels/parsers do not manufacture false-positive reachability via stale entries, redirects, parser errors or fuzzy matching (the flip side of representation loss: no false accepts).

NC_SYNTHETIC_SITEMAP_ABSENCE.expected: synthetic URLs absent from every parsed sitemap/search-index URL set on every host
NC_SYNTHETIC_SITEMAP_ABSENCE.pre_freeze_observed: absent on all 4 hosts (vitepress sitemap/hashmap, nix.dev sitemap/doc_urls, doc.rust-lang.org sitemap.txt, rust-lang.github.io channel absence) - 0 hits

NC_SYNTHETIC_PAGE_404.expected: every synthetic item page returns HTTP 404
NC_SYNTHETIC_PAGE_404.pre_freeze_observed: 404 on all 8 synthetic probes (2 per host x 4 hosts), re-certified 2026-10-10T18:14:47Z

operational_definitions.substrate: HTTP GET only via Python stdlib urllib; TLS verified; frozen User-Agent 'SPIDER-research-frontier-38013774272/1.0'; timeout 12s; max response body 600000 bytes (one exception below); redirects followed; no credentials, cookies, browser, Docker, model key or write verb. EXCEPTION: mdBook searchindex.js and sitemap artifacts are fetched with a 12000000-byte cap where needed (nix.dev searchindex.js measured 8.6 MB at DESIGN).
operational_definitions.navigation_graph: Directed graph whose nodes are canonicalized same-host http(s) URLs and whose edges are static <a href> links parsed in document order; asset extensions excluded; JS-generated links are NOT edges (disclosed VN-V2).
operational_definitions.hop_distance: Graph shortest-path length in edges from the seed root (hop 0), measured by the frozen BFS (budget B=250, depth cap D=6, each URL fetched at most once). Certified frame uses browser-correct URL resolution (certified_bfs2.json), matching item URLs in engine-native forms.
operational_definitions.state_carrying_item: A page that contains >=1 named form control: <input> with non-empty name attribute OR <select> with non-empty name attribute. The item observable is the page URL; named_controls is recorded per item.
operational_definitions.DEEP: hop in {3,4,5,6} (inherited from the parent's DEEP band; state items at hop<=2 are outside the frame). MANDATE NOTE: the mandate says DEEP = 'hop >= 3' which equals {3,4,5,6} under this chart; realized frame = hop 3 (shallow member), disclosed.
operational_definitions.canonicalization: Two distinct notions, both frozen: (a) ITEM URL FORM = the engine-native serving form as stored in target_pool.admitted_items (extensionless on vitepress.dev and nix.dev, '.html' on doc.rust-lang.org and rust-lang.github.io). EXECUTE fetches the stored form. (b) CANONICAL MATCH KEY = final URL after redirects; fragment removed, query string removed, trailing slash removed, terminal '.html'/'.htm' removed from the last path segment; applied identically to item URLs and to every channel-output URL before matching.

channel_definitions.ROBOTS_SITEMAP: GET https://<host>/robots.txt; extract Sitemap: directive URLs; GET each sitemap (gzip-decoded if .gz); if a sitemapindex, recurse into up to 12 child sitemaps; union all <loc> and plain-text URL entries; match the item's canonical match key.
channel_definitions.SITEMAP_XML: GET https://<host>/sitemap.xml and https://<host>/sitemap_index.xml directly (same recursion/gzip rules) and match. NOTE: doc.rust-lang.org returns 404 for both (only robots.txt routes to its sitemap.txt); this is a measured per-host aggregate fact, recorded in pre_freeze_control_certificate.
channel_definitions.ON_SITE_SEARCH: Two sub-mechanisms, both without JS execution: (a) STATIC FORM branch: on the seed root locate a static <form> that has an EXPLICIT action attribute and a named search-like input; construct action?param=<item last path segment>; GET results; match item URLs. Forms WITHOUT an explicit action attribute (e.g., mdBook 'searchbar-outer' forms on nix.dev/doc.rust-lang.org/rust-lang.github.io, whose default action is the page itself) are NOT invoked and yield zero output; this is a measured aggregate instrument fact. (b) STATIC INDEX branch: probe well-known static search-index artifacts referenced from or well-known relative to the seed root and parse them WITHOUT EXECUTING JS: JSON indexes (/search/search_index.json, /search-index.json, /search.json, /pagefind/pagefind-entry.json, /hashmap.json) AND JS-wrapped static index-data files whose payload is a literal JSON object/array (notably mdBook /searchindex.js containing a 'doc_urls' array). For mdBook searchindex.js the doc_urls entries are RESOLVED against the directory of the artifact before canonicalization. Artifacts whose contents are non-URL ids are recorded as measured facts (e.g., vitepress.dev /hashmap.json is present with 282 keys but its keys are '.md'-relative ids, NOT URLs, so it yields zero URL entries under the match rule). This static-.js extension is REQUIRED for two-sidedness: without it, mdBook content pages that have no content-sitemap coverage are undiscoverable by construction, which would manufacture a floor (a v1 defect). Any executed-JS or remote query endpoint (API search, Algolia, pagefind JS loader) is NOT invoked (disclosed).
channel_definitions.RSS_ATOM: Find <link rel=alternate type=application/rss+xml|application/atom+xml> on the seed root; GET the feed; match item URLs from <item><link>, <entry><link href> or <guid>. Measured at DESIGN: zero feed alternate links on all four seed roots.
channel_definitions.JSON_LD: GET the seed root as a discovery hub and enumerate same-host URLs from all <script type=application/ld+json> blocks (url/@id/mainEntityOfPage/itemListElement). ANTI-TAUTOLOGY: the item page itself is NOT used as its own JSON-LD hub (a self-fetch implementation is rejected). Measured at DESIGN: zero ld+json blocks on all four seed roots.

operational_definitions.channel_success_rule: A channel succeeds for an item iff the item's canonical match key is discovered from that channel's output AND the item page is fetched with a final 2xx within the remaining K GETs. Each 3xx redirect counts as 1 GET.
operational_definitions.union_rule: item_reachable_via_discovery = OR(channel_success over the 5 channels); each channel is probed independently per fresh episode (no cross-item caching), so an item's reachability is certified within its own K=3 episode.
operational_definitions.sampling_rule: Frozen frame = for each seed, run the frozen BFS once (budget 250, depth 6, same-host static-<a>, document order); admit text/html pages at hop in {3,4,5,6} with >=1 named control; within an engine admit up to 10 items in BFS fetch order (first-10 rule). Deterministic; the exact admitted URL list with engine-native serving forms is frozen in target_pool.admitted_items (40 items, 10 per engine).
operational_definitions.temporal_drift: EXECUTE measures discovery on the exact frozen admitted item URLs and re-runs the frozen BFS only to record hop depth and requests-to-first-reach; an admitted URL that no longer resolves at EXECUTE is excluded with a recorded reason (never counted as unreachable-by-discovery).

measurement_validity.VN-V1_substrate: Credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP; no browser, Docker, model key, credential, cookie or write verb. Identical to EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378.
measurement_validity.VN-V2_static_parser_only: HTML parsed with stdlib html.parser/regex. JS-rendered navigation and JS-executed search are NOT followed, so JS-dependent discovery channels are missed and disclosed as representation loss. Static JS-wrapped index DATA files are parsed as text without executing JS (see ON_SITE_SEARCH).
measurement_validity.VN-V3_same_host: Only same-host static navigation defines hop; cross-host navigation is out of scope, which bounds the claim to same-host acquisition on this substrate class.
measurement_validity.VN-V4_frame_certificate: The DEEP state-item frame was certified live during DESIGN across 4 distinct host engines (40 items, 10 per engine): every admitted URL returned final 2xx with the recorded named_controls on 2026-10-10, and hop=3 for all 40 (the shallow member of the DEEP band), certified from the browser-correct BFS hop maps matched in engine-native form. Pinned inline in target_pool.admitted_items (hashed inside spec.json by the freezer).
measurement_validity.VN-V5_k_budget: K=3 includes redirects and item-page fetch; it is generous for the measured channel mechanics: sitemap channels need robots+sitemap+item (3 GETs) or sitemap+item (2), the static-index branch needs seed+index+item (3), feeds need root+feed+item (3). Redirects count as GETs; all 40 admitted items served direct (final==url) so the item-page GET is 1.
measurement_validity.VN-V6_channel_independence: Channels are probed independently and reported separately; overlap (e.g., robots.txt -> sitemap) is disclosed and the union is not double-counted per item.
measurement_validity.VN-V7_no_token_cost: No tokenizer/latency/dollar model; GET requests and response-body bytes are the only cost bases; token fields are null.
measurement_validity.VN-V8_selection_bias: The frozen pool is a purposive sample of public documentation engines that pass the depth+control frame gate, not a random Web sample. The metric is explicitly conditional on these engines; generalization beyond the admitted pool is not claimed.
measurement_validity.VN-V9_bimodality_disclosure: Measured at DESIGN (aggregate instrument facts only): on this documentation-engine class, per-engine site-native discovery is close to a deterministic function of whether the engine publishes a machine-readable content index over the frame subtree. vitepress.dev publishes a page-level content sitemap (272 locs incl. locale guide pages); nix.dev's sitemap excludes the /manual/ subtree (0 of 58 locs) but it publishes a static search index (1933 doc_urls); doc.rust-lang.org publishes only a version-level sitemap.txt (3 lines, none cargo) and its book search index has 0 cargo entries; rust-lang.github.io publishes no robots/sitemap and its async-book search index covers 3 of its 10 frame items (structural max 3/10 = 0.30 < 0.50). The >=2-engine boundary is therefore concentrated on the two live engines (vitepress.dev sitemap, nix.dev static search index) and is genuinely at risk: E in {0,1,2} with E=2 REQUIRING BOTH live engines' per-item membership to materialize at EXECUTE. The known cost of this composition is reduced power to detect intermediate per-engine fractions and a tight dynamic range on E; this is disclosed as the central validity threat. The that-matters discrimination: does the only mechanism that can move the boundary (a static search index on an engine with no content-sitemap subtree coverage) actually enumerate the frozen DEEP items at EXECUTE?
measurement_validity.VN-V10_sitemap_recursion_cap: sitemapindex recursion is capped at 12 child sitemaps and URL parsing at 20000 URLs per host to bound bytes; a host exceeding the cap is recorded with the cap hit.
measurement_validity.VN-V11_temporal_drift: Live hosts can change between DESIGN and EXECUTE; the frozen URL list is measured as-is and drift is recorded rather than silently re-sampled.
measurement_validity.VN-V12_availability: If a seed host is unreachable at EXECUTE, that engine is recorded as unavailable (excluded from E with reason); network failure is never encoded as a scientific negative.
measurement_validity.VN-V13_cross_subtree_items: The doc.rust-lang.org seed (/book/) reaches sibling rust docs (/cargo/, root) at hop>=3 via the shared top navigation; these are retained as legitimate same-host DEEP state items and their cross-subtree origin is disclosed. The rust-lang.github.io seed (/async-book/) similarly reaches sibling projects (/rfcs/, /wg-async/); disclosed.
measurement_validity.VN-V14_item_url_forms: Item URLs are stored in engine-native serving forms and fetched as-is: extensionless on vitepress.dev and nix.dev; '.html' on doc.rust-lang.org and rust-lang.github.io (extensionless variants are not used). Matching always uses the canonical match key (fragment/query/slash/'.html' stripped) applied identically to items and channel outputs, so search-index '.html' entries match extensionless items and vice versa.
measurement_validity.VN-V15_hop_map_key_form: Certified hop values are read from the browser-correct BFS hop_map matching item URLs in their engine-native stored form (doc.rust-lang.org/rust-lang.github.io keys retain '.html'; nix.dev keys retain trailing slash). Canonical-form fallback is applied identically for both map lookup and channel matching, ruling out hop under- or over-counting from form mismatch.

decision_rule.primary_decision_variable: E = count over engines available at EXECUTE of (discovery_reachable_fraction_per_engine[host] >= threshold). E is the sole variable that maps to an outcome; the aggregate discovery_reachable_fraction and the per-channel fractions are reported diagnostics and are NOT themselves the decision variable.
decision_rule.primary_metric: discovery_reachable_fraction_per_engine[host] = count(admitted DEEP items of that host reachable via ANY of the five channels within K=3 GETs, per union_rule) / admitted count of that host (=10). Aggregate discovery_reachable_fraction = total reachable / 40.

mapping.SUPPORTS: E >= 2: shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier where site-native discovery channels exist; persistence of paths is not the primary optimization target; effort moves to discovery and substrate expansion.
mapping.MIXED: E == 1: exactly one engine's site-native discovery reaches >=0.50 of its DEEP frame; evidence is engine-dependent and the discovery hypothesis is only weakly supported.
mapping.FALSIFIES: E == 0: site-native discovery reaches <0.50 on every engine in <=K=3 GETs; fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound with a computable persistence break-even surface.

decision_rule.measurement_invalid_guard: If a control fails (PC channel-liveness false, NC synthetic 404 not reproduced, or denominator 0) the outcome is MEASUREMENT_INVALID with the failing control named; infrastructure failure is recorded separately and never mapped to FALSIFIES.

product_consequence_positive: If SUPPORTS (E>=2): shortest-path hop is not a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier where site-native discovery channels (content sitemap or static search index) exist; persistent path caches are not the primary optimization target for SPIDER memory; effort shifts to discovery-channel coverage, engine/index-artifact detection, hybrid discovery+traversal for unindexed engines, and substrate expansion.
product_consequence_negative: If FALSIFIES/MIXED (E<2): even with the full frozen site-native discovery toolkit, fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound on a material share of engines (the two measured index-less engines exert the floor); persistence of paths/procedures retains a real depth-dependent amortization surface whose break-even can be computed from measured re-derivation cost (re-validation GETs/bytes plus stale-replay false-accept vs re-derivation, scaling with hop and elapsed time); memory architecture should keep path/procedure persistence as a core optimization lever.

estimated_cost.http_gets_estimate: ~1400-2000 GETs total: certified BFS 4x250=1000 + discovery probing 40 items x 5 channels x <=3 GETs (worst case ~600, typically far less: sitemap engines 2-3 GETs per item, static-index engines 3 GETs per item with one index fetch amortized per episode) + channel hub/robot/sitemap/search-index fetches (~20, incl. nix.dev searchindex.js 8.6 MB) + null control 8 x 2 + frame re-certification at EXECUTE. nix.dev searchindex.js is fetched once per engine episode and re-used across that episode's items (disclosed in union_rule/channel_success accounting).
estimated_cost.bytes: dominant: nix.dev searchindex.js ~8.6 MB, doc.rust-lang.org book searchindex-3cc309c2.js ~4.7 MB, rust-lang.github.io async-book index ~1.3 MB, vitepress sitemap.xml ~250 KB; order ~20-30 MB total.
estimated_cost.latency: bounded by 12s/request timeout; total runtime minutes on one runner
estimated_cost.amortization: no persistence across episodes (fresh-agent episodes by construction)

expected_information_gain: High and decision-changing for the program-level architecture synthesis. The experiment measures, on a live-certified multi-engine DEEP frame, whether site-native discovery collapses the depth cost that motivates SPIDER's persistence architecture. SUPPORTS redirects the program from path persistence to discovery/substrate expansion; FALSIFIES/MIXED validates persistence and yields a real break-even surface for the maintenance/invalidation axis. It is the first measurement of this question (the v1 freeze was BLOCKED pre-measurement with an empty frame), so any outcome is new information.

decision_rule_reachability.reason: Denominator is fixed and non-zero: 40 admitted DEEP items, 10 per engine, all certified at hop exactly 3 with 200/direct/nc>=1 on 2026-10-10 (target_pool.admitted_items; pre_freeze_control_certificate.frame_admission_recheck). Both falsifier branches are arithmetically satisfiable with non-zero assignment mass: E=2 (SUPPORTS) requires both live engines (vitepress.dev sitemap, nix.dev search index) to enumerate their frame items; E=1 (MIXED) and E=0 (FALSIFIES) remain reachable because the frozen record contains ONLY aggregate channel scope facts (272 locs / 1933 doc_urls / 0-under-manual), never a per-item membership witness. The two structural-floor engines (doc.rust-lang.org expected 0/10; rust-lang.github.io structural max 3/10) are disclosed floors that calibrate the negative end and cannot force either outcome. No frozen fact fixes any per-engine fraction.

measurement_prerequisites.reason: All measurement prerequisites verified live during DESIGN on 2026-10-10: (1) substrate present and credentialed-free GET works (4 seed roots 200 over TLS, stdlib urllib, UA 'SPIDER-research-frontier-38013774272/1.0'); (2) DEEP frame certified to exist (4 engines x 10 items, all hop==3 from certified browser-correct BFS hop maps, all 200/direct/nc>=1); (3) at least one probeable discovery channel returns non-empty same-host URL content (positive control PC met: vitepress sitemap.xml 200/272, nix.dev searchindex.js 200/1933 doc_urls); (4) null control verified (8/8 synthetic pages 404, 0 synthetic ids in parsed URL sets); (5) gzip/sitemap handling exercised on live artifacts; (6) no code change required (measurement-only experiment, stdlib only).

baseline_identifiability.reason: Baselines are identifiable on the SAME frozen frame: B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS is computed at EXECUTE by re-running the frozen item-blind BFS (B=250, D=6, same-host static-<a>, document order) on the frozen seeds over the frozen admitted item set, yielding bfs_requests_to_first_reach[item] and hop_depth[item]; the DESIGN-time BFS that certified the frame used the identical policy (certified_bfs2.json). B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY == 1 by construction (theoretical lower bound). B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT is analytically defined and explicitly labeled inherited context never paired into the primary metric. None of the baselines shares its random seed with the discovery measurement; each engine episode is fresh-agent by construction.

control_sensitivity.reason: Both controls can genuinely fail at EXECUTE and are sensitive to the failure modes they guard: PC_DISCOVERY_CHANNEL_LIVENESS would fail if hosts rotate robots/sitemap off or block the UA (observed channel URL-set sizes range 0..272 across engines, so a dead channel is detectable), and NC_SYNTHETIC_UNREACHABLE_ITEM would fail if parsers manufacture false positives (e.g., fuzzy matching returning a synthetic id, redirect-based 200s, or stale index entries) - 8/8 synthetic 404s and 0 id hits currently pass, and a single false accept fails the control. Both statuses are re-checkable at EXECUTE independently of the primary metric.

treatment_liveness.reason: This Frontier experiment has NO SPIDER product-code treatment arm: it is a pure measurement of the frozen site-native discovery channel procedures under the credential-free GET substrate. The 'treatment' under test - the five channel procedures (ROBOTS_SITEMAP, SITEMAP_XML, ON_SITE_SEARCH static branches, RSS_ATOM, JSON_LD) implemented with stdlib GET - was exercised LIVE during DESIGN on the exact frozen pool: robots.txt and sitemaps fetched 200 on 3 hosts, search-index artifacts fetched 200 (nix.dev searchindex.js 8.6MB, doc.rust-lang.org book index, rust-lang.github.io async-book index), and the null-control probes returned 404 (8/8), with zero JS execution and zero credentials, exactly as frozen. Channels are therefore demonstrably alive before freeze; EXECUTE needs no new code, only re-execution of the frozen procedures.

freeze_artifacts_bound.reason: This experiment has NO mutable local code, task bank, dataset or fixture whose identity could change interpretation: substrate is Python stdlib only (no repo code is modified or added; measurement-only experiment), the target pool and the complete pre-freeze control certificate are embedded INLINE in spec.json (which freeze.json hashes as a canonical packet file), and DESIGN-stage scope (check_scope.py design exact list) permits writing ONLY the listed text files, so no separate artifact file can or should be created. The inline certificate therefore IS the bound artifact: its hash integrity is carried by freeze.json.hashes['spec.json']. freeze_artifacts is [] accordingly.
